results: 1. Detailed neurological examination including assessment of voluntary eye movements, doll's head maneuver (oculocephalic reflex), and convergence testing

video-oculography / eye-movement recording: normal baseline vertical saccades and gaze; dose-related conjugate upward eye deviation with blepharospasm beginning about 30 minutes after levodopa and resolving by 3 hours
vertical saccades and gaze range (up and down): NO baseline oculomotor abnormality before levodopa - the upward deviation is drug-induced, not a supranuclear palsy
smooth pursuit and saccade velocity: normal
2. Serum ceruloplasmin and 24-hour urine copper levels
3. MRI of the brain with attention to the basal ganglia and midbrain
MRI brain - midbrain (hummingbird sign, midbrain-to-pons ratio): no hummingbird sign
MRI brain - putamen (atrophy, rim sign, hot cross bun, SWI hypointensity): putaminal atrophy with the rim sign and putaminal hypointensity on susceptibility-weighted imaging
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Levodopa-induced oculogyric crisis in a patient with Multiple System Atrophy (MSA-P)
Alternative 1: Idiopathic adult-onset dystonia presenting as oculogyric crisis
Alternative 2: Wilson's disease
